exception.note: No exception applies; the way out is to fix the finding, `exclude` for generated code, or the code itself.

summary: An HTTP request or client built without a timeout.
allowed: Give the call a deadline: `HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))` (java.net.http), `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` on an `HttpURLConnection`, a client with timeouts (OkHttp, which sets them by default, or Ktor with `install(HttpTimeout) { requestTimeoutMillis = 10_000 }`), `RestTemplateBuilder().connectTimeout(...).readTimeout(...)` for Spring, or `RequestConfig.custom().setResponseTimeout(...)` for the Apache client. This HTTP call has no timeout, so a server that never answers hangs it for good.

summary: SQL text built from a runtime value with a template, `+` or `format`.
allowed: Pass values as bind parameters: `jdbcTemplate.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?", mapper, id)`, `prepareStatement("... WHERE id = ?")` with `setLong(1, id)`, `:id` with `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate` or JPA `setParameter("id", id)`, or a query DSL (Exposed, jOOQ). Build placeholder lists from placeholders alone (`ids.joinToString(", ") { "?" }`), optional filters from literal fragments joined with `" AND "`, and take a table or column name from a constant or an enum. This SQL text is built from a runtime value with a string template, `+` or `format`, so the value can change the statement (SQL injection).

summary: TLS certificate or host-name verification switched off.
allowed: Keep certificate and host-name verification on and trust the certificate authority instead: load it into a `KeyStore` and build the `SSLContext` from `TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm()).apply { init(keyStore) }`, use OkHttp `HandshakeCertificates.Builder().addTrustedCertificate(certificate)`, or set `-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore` for a private CA. This trusts any certificate or host name, so anyone on the network can pose as the server, and turning it off by environment ships the switch to production.

summary: Deserialization that instantiates attacker-chosen types (`XMLDecoder`, default typing, Kryo without registration).
allowed: Read the data as JSON into a concrete type: `Json.decodeFromString<Order>(text)` with kotlinx.serialization or `mapper.readValue<Order>(text)` with Jackson, with polymorphism by a logical name (a `sealed` class with kotlinx.serialization, or `@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)` with `@JsonSubTypes`). This reads class names or objects from the data, so a crafted payload builds any class on the classpath and runs code.

summary: MD2, MD4, MD5 or SHA-1 for hashing or signing, or HMAC-MD5.
allowed: Hash with `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")` (or SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256), sign with `Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256")`, and hash passwords with Argon2 or bcrypt (`Argon2PasswordEncoder`, `BCryptPasswordEncoder`): MD5 and SHA-1 are broken hashes, collisions are cheap and brute force is fast. A protocol you do not control that requires one (a legacy signature, an ETag, a WebSocket accept key) is the exception.

summary: A file is not formatted with ktfmt
why: When the project formats with ktfmt, the format check reports every file it would change.
allowed: Run ktfmt on the file; it fixes the layout.

summary: A ktlint formatting rule
why: When the project formats with ktlint, the format check reports each rule of the ktlint standard ruleset that a file breaks.
allowed: Run `ktlint --format` on the file; it fixes the layout. Not your formatter: set `kotlin.formatter` in nitpicker.config.json.
